title: ci(suite-ceilings): a new package is not red before its first ceiling
body:
Fixes #16468
Clause-②: no

Implements ruling Q2 B on the suite-duration ratchet (https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/16468#issuecomment-6082629070): a package absent from the ceiling dataset is a new package. It prints "no ceiling: new package" and is not red. The first refresh after it lands enters it in the dataset. A package the dataset knows but that lost its row stays red. Q1 A needs no code (the hold is as built). Part 1 of the ratchet landed as PR #22480 (`6abd265320`).

## What changed

`scripts/check-test-suite-ceilings.mjs`:

- **Grading.** A package absent from the dataset with no ruled entry now gets row status `new` (it was `absent`). `RED_STATUSES` is `over` alone, so the exit code follows only an over-ceiling package or a refusal.
- **Rendering.** The row prints `-- no ceiling: new package (not in scripts/test-shard-timings.json; the first refresh after it lands enters it)`, in the same column as the `provisional` and `carried` rows. The red header, the red detail and the error annotation lose their absent-package branch, because no red row can lack a ceiling now.
- **"Lost its row" stays red** (see the finding below). `readCeilingTable` already refused a weight with neither a ceiling nor an `uncapped` reason. It now also refuses a ceiling, an `uncapped` reason or a `provisional` mark that names a package with no weight. Without this, that shape would have changed from red (as built, it graded `absent`) to "no ceiling: new package".
- **Prose the ruling made false**, prose only. The header bullet now states the ruled rule and cites the ruling URL. Also updated: the NOT MEASURED paragraph, the exit-code table, the `gradeCeilings` status table and the `RULED_CEILING_RAISES` comment ("the only way a package that has never landed can get one").

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: the comment above `Check the per-package suite-duration ceilings` said "a package absent from the dataset is red (the new-package shape)". It now states the ruled rule. Comment only, no step change.

Sweep for other sentences stating the old rule: `git grep -n -i -E "absent from the dataset|new-package shape|new package|ruled raise|no ceiling"` over the tree found only ci.yml lines 1462-1463, and they are fixed here. The ceiling prose in `.github/workflows/shard-timings-refresh.yml` and `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` describes the hold and the formula, not the new-package rule, so it is untouched. Neither file is in this diff, and neither is `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` or `scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs`.

## The inverted pin

The battery `'a package absent from the dataset is red; an uncapped one is not'` (floor 4) is now `'a new package prints "no ceiling: new package" and is not red; a known one that lost its row is refused'` (floor 10):

1. A new package (9999 s) beside one within its ceiling: row status `new`, exit 0, verdict `OK`.
2. The printed text is `brand-new: 5.00s -- no ceiling: new package`.
3. Beside a package over its ceiling: exit 1, the header counts 1 package, and the single error annotation does not name the new package.
4. A new package alone: `NOT MEASURED`, exit 0.
5. and 6. The `uncapped` half is kept: a `carried` package is not red and its reason is printed.
7. to 10. A known package that lost its row is refused. Covered: a weight with no ceiling or reason; a ceiling with no weight; an `uncapped` reason with no weight; a `provisional` mark with no weight. Each case asserts the refusal text names the package.

The ruled-raise battery gains one case (floor 7 to 8), which measures dispatch assumption 6. A ruled entry for a new package still gives it a ceiling that it can run over: 31 s against a ruled 30 s reads `over`, exit 1. The existing case (5 s against a ruled 30 s reads `ok`) is reworded to the new meaning.

`node scripts/check-test-suite-ceilings.mjs --self-test`: `self-test OK (42 cases across 7 batteries)`, up from 35. Exit 0 at `791aaf55`.

## Ablation

The fix was committed first (`791aaf55`). Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the anchor had to hit once, the blob had to change on disk, and the restore was proven as blob == `HEAD` (`570a0ceaa046`) with `git diff HEAD` empty. These are root scripts with no `dist/`, so no build leg applies.

| leg | mutation | self-test |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `RED_STATUSES = new Set(['over', 'new'])` (the PM's ablation) | exit 1. Red, but via a `TypeError` in the red renderer (`r.ceiling` is null), thrown inside the inverted battery's first case. |
| 1b | leg 1, plus the red detail and annotation filtered to rows with a ceiling: the as-built semantic restored without the crash | exit 1, by the pin's own assertion: `new: exit 1, verdict OVER, new` |
| 2 | the weightless refusal disabled (its `if` short-circuited with `false &&`) | exit 1: `lost row: a ceiling with no weight was graded as new (null)` |
| 2b | `provisional` dropped from the weightless set | exit 1: `lost row: a provisional mark with no weight was graded as new (null)` |
| 2c | `uncapped` dropped from the weightless set | exit 1: `lost row: an uncapped reason with no weight was graded as new (null)` |
| 3 | the printed text reverted to `no ceiling: not in ...` | exit 1: `new: the line is wrong` |

Leg 1's direction is red, as expected, but the crash fires before the pin's assertions run. Leg 1b is there so that the inverted assertion itself is what fails.

## Finding: where a package the dataset knows could be graded as new (dispatch assumption 2)

Searched: every path in `gradeCeilings` / `readCeilingTable` that yields "not in the dataset", and every path in the generator (`suiteCeilings`, `buildDataset`, `provisionalPackages` in `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs`) and the refresh lane (`shard-timings-refresh.yml`, `coverageReport` in `scripts/ci/select-shard-timings-run.mjs`) that can remove a package's row.

- **A weight with no ceiling and no `uncapped` reason.** Already refused, as the PM expected. It is now pinned in the inverted battery as well.
- **A ceiling, an `uncapped` reason or a `provisional` mark with no weight.** This was NOT refused. The grader keys "in the dataset" on `packages` alone, so before this change it graded `absent` (red). A bare Q2 change would have graded it `new` (not red) and ignored the ceiling the table holds. The generator never writes this shape: `suiteCeilings` iterates `packages`, and `provisional` is a subset of executed plus carried, which is `packages`. So only a hand edit reaches it, and it is now refused like its mirror. Probe: a first table built by the generator's own `suiteCeilings` over the live dataset (72 weights, 71 ceilings, 1 `uncapped: provisional`) passes the reader. A new package graded against it prints the new line, exit 0.
- **The generator dropping a held ceiling.** `suiteCeilings` drops a prior ceiling whose package left `packages`, and the next executing refresh would set a fresh one. The refresh lane closes this for a package that still exists. `coverageReport` names any package the committed dataset weighs, which the workspace still contains, but which the refresh no longer covers. The workflow then exits 1 with "NOTHING was regenerated and no PR was opened". What can still drop is a package that left the workspace: deleted, or renamed, and a rename's new name is exactly the "new or renamed" case Q2 B rules not red. `@objectstack/dogfood` is excluded from coverage, but ci.yml excludes it from Test Core, so it is never graded. The residual is in Acceptance notes.

## Q1 A, as built (no code, per the ruling)

The effective ceiling is `max(generated, ruled entry)`. A `RULED_CEILING_RAISES` entry below the generated ceiling therefore lowers nothing: the verdict lists it under "changing nothing (delete them)". So the ruling's parenthetical "a lowering is a ruled entry too" has no as-built mechanism. Nothing about lowering was changed here.

## Verification at `791aaf55`

- `node scripts/check-test-suite-ceilings.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, 42 cases across 7 batteries. On the base (`35ef501e13`) it read 35 across 7.
- `node scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, unchanged.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, with no paths (it derives the change set from the merge base, 2 paths): 58 commands. 53 exit 0. Four exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, they read built `dist/`): `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`. These four are declared NOT MEASURED. None of them reads `ci.yml` (only doc comments name it), the diff touches no package's `files[]`, and the shared turbo cache is cold. CI runs them after Build Core.
- `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` was run detached, as its header prescribes, and read from its log: `✓ dispatch-gates self-test: 2011 cases pass.` It took 1377.4 s on this box, with no lifecycle failure line.
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: 58 derived families, 54 run, 4 NOT-MEASURED (derived from the recorded exit 3), 0 UNRUN.
- Lint, a proven narrowing rather than a repo-wide run. (1) Population: `eslint --print-config` for the touched script resolves 2 rules and no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, and the `files` glob does not cover `.yml`. (2) Count: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` read 1 file, with 0 errors and 0 warnings. (3) Invariance: type-aware linting is not enabled, so this diff cannot move any other file's verdict.

## Acceptance notes

- Noted, not filed. A refresh run by hand with the generator's documented command (`provenance.refresh`) has no coverage check. It can therefore drop a still-existing package's held ceiling with its weight. After that, the package would grade as new and the next refresh would set a fresh ceiling. The lane workflow refuses this, and no hand-run refresh has happened. Carrier: whoever next touches `suiteCeilings` or the refresh lane.
